stem.text: Let f and g be continuous functions with \( \int_{0}^{6} f(x)\,dx = 9 \), \( \int_{2}^{6} f(x)\,dx = 4 \), and \( \int_{2}^{0} g(x)\,dx = -5 \). Find the value of \( \int_{0}^{2} \left(3f(x) - g(x)\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the given integral of g: \( \int_{0}^{2} g(x)\,dx = -(-5) = 5 \), and use linearity on the requested integral.

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, one supplied integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: a linear combination of two functions

distractor_derivations.A: given integral of g from 2 to 0 used as if it ran from 0 to 2
distractor_derivations.C: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral of f from 0 to 2 as 4 - (9)
distractor_derivations.D: integral of f from 6 to 2 taken as 4 instead of -4
